posture_reason: Highest assessed path risk is medium across 3 of 5 paths; 2 paths could not be assessed with the evidence available.
executive_summary: Example Manufacturing uses generative AI. 6 AI services are connected to Entra and 88 users have granted them access.
No local model runners were found in the endpoint software inventory.
Network traffic to AI services and data-exposure signals could not be assessed from the evidence available, so the posture reflects only the paths that were measured.

paths.headline: 3 third-party AI services found in Entra (ChatGPT / OpenAI, Otter.ai, Read AI); 88 users have granted access.
Not assessed: no archived report carries proxy, DNS or firewall traffic to AI services.
No local model runners; AI desktop apps (Grammarly, Notion AI) on up to 8 hosts of 788 inventoried hosts.
Not assessed: no DLP source on this tenant.
0 enabled rule(s) specific to AI use; 2 generic consent rule(s).

findings.title: Consumer-grade AI services connected to the tenant
findings.detail: Otter.ai (Tier 1: may keep or train on prompts) have been granted access by 5 users without a verified publisher.

findings.title: Widely used AI service with no approved-AI list
findings.detail: ChatGPT / OpenAI (83 users) is connected for users across the organization. No approved-AI list was supplied, so the service is reported as unverified rather than unsanctioned.

findings.title: AI desktop applications installed
findings.detail: Grammarly (8 hosts), Notion AI (1 host) are installed, the most common on 8 hosts.

findings.title: No detection is specific to AI use
findings.detail: 2 generic consent rule(s) exist, but nothing alerts on a new AI service, an AI-classified consent or a local model runner.

recommendations.title: Review and revoke unverified AI grants
recommendations.detail: Confirm the business need for each Tier 1 service; revoke the grant and require admin consent for new AI apps.

recommendations.title: Publish an approved-AI list
recommendations.detail: Record which AI services are approved, at which tier and for which data, so use can be reported as sanctioned or not.

recommendations.title: Add AI desktop apps to the software policy
recommendations.detail: State which AI clients are approved; remove the rest through the endpoint tool.

recommendations.title: Enable the proposed AI detections
recommendations.detail: Add the detections listed in this report so new AI adoption is seen as it happens.

detections_to_add.name: New OAuth consent to an AI-classified app
detections_to_add.logic: Office365 'Consent to application' where the target app matches the AI catalog

detections_to_add.name: Local LLM runner installed
detections_to_add.logic: Software inventory delta where a name matches Ollama, LM Studio, GPT4All, Jan, llama.cpp, koboldcpp, text-generation-webui or LocalAI

coverage_gaps: Granted permission names are not in the application dump for some AI apps (only ids): high-risk scope checks cover apps whose permissions are named.
Per-user grants are matched by application name; grant scopes and consent time are not in the user dump.
Network egress (proxy, DNS, firewall) to AI services is not assessed: no archived report carries it.
Data exposure (DLP matches coinciding with AI use) is not assessed: no DLP source; bulk downloads are only context.
